items.title: Data foundation & seed
items.goal: The seventeen-table schema exists with Row Level Security on every table and no public policy, CV files live in a private bucket reached only through short-lived signed links, Singapore working days are computable in SQL and TypeScript, and a developer can rebuild the entire fictional dataset from the sample-data store with one command.
prd: Data model (suggested) → 17 core tables; scores keyed to job version and model version → suggested
Security (suggested) → RLS on every table with no public policies; private bucket with short-lived signed links → suggested
Pipeline tracking → limits count working days, Monday to Friday, skipping Singapore public holidays → decided
Main flows → Seeding (MVP): load sample CVs through the real parser, score them, back-date stage entries → suggested
Non-functional requirements → MVP data: 200 fictional CVs (about 20 in Simplified Chinese) and 20 sample jobs → decided
Free-tier limits → no backups; re-seed from the repo → decided
exit: Every table has RLS enabled with no public policy, proven by a test showing the publishable key reads nothing
CV files open only through short-lived signed URLs from server code
Working-day arithmetic agrees between the SQL function and its TypeScript mirror on every edge case in the test list
`npm run seed` rebuilds the dataset from scratch and is safe to re-run
outOfScope: Real candidate data of any kind — the seed loads fictional files only
Backups and point-in-time recovery — not in the MVP
Duplicate detection — a non-goal; resubmissions become separate candidates and are only logged
Consent and retention columns beyond what the model defines for the real-data release

items.title: The core schema exists with RLS locked down
items.story: As the agency director, I want the database unreachable from the browser and every table locked down by default, so that a portal with no sign-in still cannot leak a single row.
ac: Given the migrations are applied to an empty database, when I list the tables, then all seventeen exist with the columns the data-model record specifies.
Given the publishable key, when it queries any table, then it returns no rows and no error that reveals the schema.
Given a match score, when it is stored, then its key includes the candidate, the job version and the model version.
Given a recruiter edit to a parsed field, when the CV is parsed again, then the edit is stored separately and is not overwritten.
prd: Data model (suggested) → the 17 tables → suggested
Data model → match scores keyed to job version and model version → decided as an invariant
Data model → candidate_profiles: recruiter edits stored separately so re-parsing never overwrites them → suggested
Security (suggested) → RLS on every table, no public policies, publishable key reads nothing → suggested

items.title: Migration: clients, jobs, job_versions and gap_flags
items.what: Create the job side of the model: client companies with their own stage limits and guarantee period, job requests with an owner name and current version, every saved job version, and the gap flags raised against a job.
scope: `clients`: name, guarantee period in days defaulting to 30, optional stage-limit overrides
`jobs`: client, owner name, status, current job version
`job_versions`: the job's fields, must-have and nice-to-have requirements, and the written reason when nationality or language is required
`gap_flags`: type (missing, uncertain, conflicting, fair-employment), why it matters, the suggested client question, resolution state and note
RLS enabled on all four with no policy
Regenerated database types
done: The four tables apply cleanly to an empty database and the migration is reversible
`job_versions` cannot store a nationality or language requirement without a written reason, enforced by a constraint
RLS is enabled on all four tables and no policy is created
Generated types are committed and typecheck
verify: supabase migration up on a clean database

items.title: Migration: candidates, cv_files, candidate_profiles and candidate_skills
items.what: Create the candidate side of the model, keeping recruiter edits in their own columns or rows so that re-parsing a CV never overwrites them, and keeping every skill tied to the CV text it came from.
scope: `candidates`: contact details, plus the consent-status, consent-date and last-activity columns the real-data release will need
`cv_files`: storage path, source reference, source hash, language, parse status and error reason
`candidate_profiles`: parsed fields and, stored separately, the recruiter's overrides with who typed them and when
`candidate_skills`: skill, and the exact CV text it came from
RLS enabled on all four with no policy
Regenerated database types
done: Parsed values and recruiter overrides occupy separate, independently readable storage
Every `candidate_skills` row requires its source text; a row without it is rejected
RLS is enabled on all four tables with no policy
Generated types are committed and typecheck
verify: supabase migration up on a clean database

items.title: Migration: embeddings with pgvector and match_scores keyed by job and model version
items.what: Create the matching storage: pgvector embeddings for CVs and job versions, and match scores keyed so an old score can never be shown against a changed job.
scope: Enable the `vector` extension
`embeddings`: owner type (CV or job version), owner id, the vector, and the embedding model id
`match_scores`: candidate, job version, model version, score, matched/missing/uncertain skills with their evidence quotes, and the run that produced it
A unique key over candidate, job version and model version
An index suited to the similarity search the matching phase will run
RLS enabled on both with no policy
done: The unique key over candidate, job version and model version is enforced, proven by a DB test that a duplicate is rejected
The embedding dimension and model id are stored with each vector
RLS is enabled on both tables with no policy
Generated types are committed and typecheck

items.title: Migration: pipeline_entries, stage_events, stage_limits, placements, settings_log and ai_runs
items.what: Create the pipeline, audit and AI-traceability tables: where each candidate sits on each job, every stage change with the name the recruiter typed, the limits at three levels, placements with the guarantee, the settings change log, and one row per AI call.
scope: `pipeline_entries`: candidate, job, current stage, when it was entered, owner name
`stage_events`: every change with from-stage, to-stage, the typed recruiter name and the timestamp
`stage_limits`: working-day limits at default, client and job level
`placements`: start date check and guarantee end date
`settings_log`: every settings change with the typed name
`ai_runs`: what the call read, model and version, prompt version, output, cost and duration
A constraint that a candidate sits in exactly one stage per job
RLS enabled on all six with no policy
done: A candidate cannot occupy two stages on the same job, enforced and proven by a DB test
Every `stage_events` and `settings_log` row requires a non-empty typed name
`ai_runs` stores model id, version, cost and duration as non-null for a completed run
RLS is enabled on all six tables with no policy

items.title: Prove RLS is on for every table and the publishable key reads nothing
items.what: Add the lock-down test the security baseline requires: for every table in the schema, Row Level Security is enabled, no policy grants public access, and a client using the publishable key reads zero rows. Test-first, and it must fail if a future migration adds a table without RLS.
scope: Failing tests first: enumerate every table from the catalogue and assert RLS is enabled and policy count is zero
A read attempt per table with the publishable key returning no rows
The test discovers tables dynamically, so a new table without RLS fails automatically
Wired into `npm run test:db` and the CI database job
exclusions: Adding any policy — the MVP has none
done: The test enumerates tables from the database rather than a hard-coded list
A deliberately added table without RLS makes the test fail
The publishable key returns zero rows for every table
The test runs in the CI database job

items.title: CV files are stored privately and open only through short-lived links
items.story: As a recruiter, I want to open a candidate's original CV from their profile, without that file being reachable by anyone who guesses a URL.
ac: Given the storage bucket, when it is inspected, then it is private and has no public read policy.
Given a recruiter opens a CV, when the link is generated, then it is a signed URL that expires after a short, documented lifetime.
Given an expired signed URL, when it is used, then the file is not served.
prd: Security (suggested) → CV files sit in a private bucket and open through short-lived signed links → suggested
CV processing → parsed profile: link to the original file, which is always kept → approved
Data model → cv_files: files in Storage with parse status and errors → suggested

items.title: Create the private CV bucket and the server-side signed-URL helper
items.what: Create the private Storage bucket for original CV and job-description files, and a server-only helper that issues short-lived signed URLs. Test-first: expiry and the refusal to sign anything outside the bucket are logic.
scope: A migration creating the private bucket with no public access
`src/server/storage.ts` marked `import "server-only"`: upload, and sign a path for a short documented lifetime
Failing tests first: a signed URL expires; signing rejects a path outside the bucket; the helper cannot be imported from client code
Upload validation: allowed types and the Supabase Free 50 MB per-file ceiling
exclusions: Serving files through the app rather than through signed URLs
done: The bucket is private with no public policy, proven by a DB test
Failing-then-passing tests cover expiry, path rejection and client-import refusal
Uploads over the documented size limit or of a disallowed type are rejected with a clear reason

items.title: Working days follow the Singapore calendar
items.story: As a recruiter, I want a candidate who entered a stage on Friday afternoon not to be called overdue on Monday morning, so that the delay dashboard tells me about real delays rather than about weekends.
ac: Given a stage entered on a Friday, when Monday arrives, then one working day has elapsed, not three.
Given a Singapore public holiday, when it falls inside a stage, then it does not count towards the limit.
Given a timestamp stored in UTC, when working days are counted, then the day boundary used is Singapore local midnight.
Given the same inputs, when the SQL function and the TypeScript mirror both compute working days, then they agree.
prd: Pipeline tracking → Time limits (decided): limits count working days, Monday to Friday, skipping Singapore public holidays → decided
Data model → sg_public_holidays: Singapore public holidays used for working-day counts → suggested
Main flows → Delay status: a database view works it out; no scheduled job → suggested

items.title: Add the sg_public_holidays table and seed the relevant years
items.what: Create the public-holiday table and load the Singapore public holidays for the years the MVP and its back-dated sample data touch, so working-day counts have real data from day one.
scope: `sg_public_holidays`: date, name, and the year it belongs to, with a unique key on the date
A migration or seed loading the gazetted Singapore public holidays for the years the sample data spans
RLS enabled with no policy
A note on who maintains the list once recruiters can edit it in Settings
exclusions: The Settings screen for editing holidays (E10-S02-T01)
done: The table exists with a unique key on the date and RLS enabled
The holidays for every year the sample data spans are loaded and the count is asserted by a DB test
Loading the holidays twice does not create duplicates

items.title: Write the working-day functions in SQL and TypeScript with edge-case tests
items.what: Implement working-day arithmetic twice — as a SQL function the delay view will use, and as a TypeScript mirror the app and its tests use — and prove they agree. This is the arithmetic every delay, due-soon and guarantee date depends on, so it is strictly test-first.
scope: SQL: working days elapsed between two timestamps, and the date N working days after a date, both skipping weekends and holidays
A TypeScript mirror with the same signatures

Failing tests first for: Friday entry, Saturday and Sunday entry, the eve of a holiday, the holiday itself, a run of consecutive holidays, and the 23:59 vs 00:00 Singapore boundary (15:59 vs 16:00 UTC)
A cross-check test asserting SQL and TypeScript agree over a range of dates
The rounding rule for partial days stated in the code and the tests
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover every edge case listed above, with frozen Singapore time
A cross-check test proves the SQL function and the TypeScript mirror return identical results
The day boundary used is Singapore local midnight, proven by the 15:59 / 16:00 UTC test
The rounding rule is stated once and tested

items.title: Developers can rebuild all sample data with one command
items.story: As a developer, I want `npm run seed` to rebuild the whole fictional dataset from the sample-data store through the real parser, so that the MVP has a believable database from day one and, with no backups, we can always get back to a known state.
ac: Given the sample-data store, when the seed runs, then it lists the store, downloads each file, and reports counts by type and language plus every file it skipped and why.
Given the seed has run once, when it runs again with nothing changed, then it makes no duplicate rows and reports what it skipped.
Given a file whose content changed, when the seed runs again, then it re-parses that file and the recruiter's overrides survive.
Given the seeded database, when a recruiter opens the dashboard, then on-track, due-soon and overdue candidates all appear, because stage entries were back-dated.
prd: Non-functional requirements → MVP data: 200 fictional CVs (about 20 in Simplified Chinese) and 20 sample jobs, preloaded by developers → decided
CV processing → Intake: developers run the sample CVs through the real parser → decided
Main flows → Seeding: upload, parse, embed, score, back-date stage entries → suggested
Pipeline tracking → delay detection 6: sample candidates loaded with back-dated stage dates → proposed
Free-tier limits → no backups; re-seed from the repo → decided
Non-goals → duplicate detection; resubmissions in the sample set become separate candidates

items.title: Add the seed environment guard for the sample-data store
items.what: Before anything is downloaded, make it impossible for the seed to touch the wrong store or to leak its address. The store's listing token and base URL are read from the environment, never committed, and every listed file's URL must start with the configured base or the seed aborts. Test-first.
scope: Read the listing token and the base URL by name from the environment; both are absent from the repository and from `.env.example` values
Failing tests first: a listed URL outside the configured base aborts the run; a missing variable aborts with a message naming the variable and no value
A hard rule in code and comment: the seed and eval only list and download; they never write to the store
A check that `src/` never imports the blob client
exclusions: Anything that writes to the sample-data store
Committing the base URL, the token, or any file from the store
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover the wrong-store abort and the missing-variable abort
No base URL, token or file from the store appears anywhere in the repository
A lint or test check fails if application code under `src/` imports the blob client
verify: git diff | grep -iE 'blob.vercel-storage|BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN=.'   # must be empty

items.title: Seed step: list, download, hash and convert the sample files
items.what: Walk the flat sample-data store, download each file to a gitignored cache, hash it, skip anything that is not a supported document, and convert legacy `.doc` files here — because serverless functions cannot run the converter.
scope: Paginated listing, keeping path, URL, size and upload time
Download to `.seed-cache/` (gitignored) and compute the SHA-256 of each file
Skip anything that is not PDF, DOC or DOCX, with a logged reason
Convert `.doc` to a format the parser can read, in the seed script
A run report: counts by type and by detected language, and every skipped file with its reason
done: A run over the store downloads every supported file and reports counts by type and language
Unsupported files are skipped with a reason and never silently dropped
Legacy `.doc` files are converted and readable by the parser
`.seed-cache/` is gitignored and nothing from it is committed

items.title: Seed step: classify each file as a CV or a job description by content
items.what: The store is flat and file names are inconsistent, so CVs and job descriptions must be told apart by what is inside them. Choose the method in the spec — heuristics, a classification call, or both — and report anything that cannot be classified confidently rather than guessing. Test-first.
scope: A classifier returning CV, job description, or unclassified with a confidence
Failing tests first over fictional English and Simplified Chinese fixtures of both kinds, plus an ambiguous fixture that must come back unclassified
Unclassified files are reported and skipped, never guessed
If a model call is used, it goes through the standard AI wrapper and is logged
exclusions: Parsing the CV or extracting the job description (E04, E05)
Deciding the method in this issue — the task's spec records the choice
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover English CV, Chinese CV, job description and an ambiguous file
An unclassifiable file is reported with its name and reason and is not loaded
The chosen method is recorded in the task's spec with its accuracy on the fixtures

items.title: Seed step: upload, parse, embed, load jobs, gap check and score
items.what: Run the classified files through the real application code paths: upload originals to the private bucket, parse CVs with the real parser, create embeddings, turn job descriptions into jobs and job versions, run the gap check, and score every CV against every job.
scope: Upload each original to the private Supabase Storage bucket and record it in `cv_files`
Parse CVs through the same service the app uses, writing `ai_runs`
Create embeddings for CVs and job versions
Load job descriptions into jobs and job versions, then run the gap check
Score candidates against every job, following the retrieval rule of top 50 per job
Progress output and a summary of AI calls and cost
exclusions: Writing the parser, extractor, gap check or scorer — this task orchestrates them
done: A full run produces candidates, profiles, skills with source text, embeddings, jobs, job versions, gap flags and match scores
Every AI call made by the seed appears in `ai_runs` with its model, version, cost and duration
The run prints a summary with counts per stage of the pipeline and the total AI cost

items.title: Seed step: back-date pipeline entries so delays show from day one
items.what: Give the sample candidates stage histories with entry times in the past, spread so that on-track, due-soon and overdue all appear on the dashboard the first time a recruiter opens it, along with some candidates in end states and some placed.
scope: Back-dated `pipeline_entries` and matching `stage_events`, each with a typed name that is clearly a sample value
A spread that guarantees at least one candidate in each of on track, due soon and overdue, across more than one stage and more than one client
Some candidates in each end state and some placed with a start date, so placements and the guarantee countdown have data
A DB test asserting all three delay statuses are present after seeding
exclusions: Placement records beyond what the guarantee countdown needs (E09)
done: After a seed run, the database contains at least one candidate in each of on track, due soon and overdue, proven by a DB test
End states and placed candidates are represented
Every stage event carries a sample typed name and no real person's name appears

items.title: Make the seed idempotent and add a reset command
items.what: Make re-running the seed safe: key each file by its store path with its SHA-256, skip anything unchanged, re-parse anything whose hash changed while keeping recruiter overrides, and add a reset command that clears the data so a rebuild starts clean. Test-first.
scope: Idempotency key: the file's store path in `cv_files.source_ref` with its SHA-256 in `cv_files.source_hash`
Failing tests first: unchanged hash skips; changed hash re-parses; a recruiter override survives the re-parse; a second full run creates no duplicate rows
A reset command that truncates the seeded data in dependency order and is refused against anything but a local or development database
Run summary: created, skipped, re-parsed
exclusions: Deleting anything from the sample-data store
done: Failing-then-passing tests cover skip, re-parse, override survival and no-duplicates
A second consecutive `npm run seed` reports everything skipped and changes no row count
The reset command refuses to run against a non-development database
verify: npm run seed && npm run seed

items.title: Seed run report: counts, skipped files and likely resubmissions
items.what: Produce one written report per seed run so gaps in the sample set are visible: counts of CVs by language, job descriptions, files skipped with reasons, and the files that look like resubmissions of the same person — logged only, because duplicate detection is a non-goal.
scope: A Markdown and JSON report written to a gitignored path, plus a short console summary
Counts: CVs by detected language, job descriptions, unclassified, skipped by reason
Likely resubmissions listed for the later duplicate-rule decision, with no merging or deduplication
A note comparing the counts against the PRD target of 200 CVs (about 20 Simplified Chinese) and 20 jobs, so a partial set is obvious
exclusions: Merging or deduplicating candidates — an explicit non-goal
Committing the report or any file name from the store
done: A seed run writes a report with all the counts listed above and prints a summary
Likely resubmissions are listed without any record being merged
The report states how far the current set is from the PRD target
The report path is gitignored and nothing from the store is committed
